paragraphs.text: Because you do not feel what you speak, you think the whole stands in words, and so flatter yourselves as though no one else knew anything, or could know except you.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: He reproves his friends for two faults: one, that they thought they had better knowledge than they did: and the other, that instead of true consolation, they derided and despised their friend in his adversity.
paragraphs.label: b
paragraphs.anchor: as one mocked of his neighbour

paragraphs.text: Who being a mocker and a wicked man, thinks that no man is in God's favour but he, because he has all things that he desires.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: As the rich do not esteem a light or torch that goes out, so he despised he that falls from prosperity to adversity.
paragraphs.label: d
paragraphs.anchor: He that is ready to slip

paragraphs.text: He declares to them that disputed against him, that their wisdom is common to all, and such as the very brute beasts teach daily.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He exhorts them to be wise in judging, and as well to know the right use of their God-given ears, as well as their mouths.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Though men by age and continuance of time attain wisdom, yet it is not comparable to God's wisdom, nor able to comprehend his judgments, in which he answers to that which was alleged, Job 8:8.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: He shows that there is nothing done in this world without God's will and ordinance, else he would not be Almighty.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: He abates the humour of princes, and brings them into the subjection of others.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: He causes their words to have no credit, which is when he will punish sin.
paragraphs.label: l

paragraphs.text: In this discourse of God's wonderful works, Job shows that whatever is done in this world both in the order and change of things, is by God's will and appointment, in which he declares that he thinks well of God, and is able to set forth his power in words as they that reasoned against him were.
paragraphs.label: m
